- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in the following 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3–5 days of high prices); add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for days 20–30.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +, -, +), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% bias toward true sentiment direction for next 5–7 days.
